mostWorthwhile.text: Following iron from worn red cells into marrow was most worthwhile: it showed how material can be reused to help make replacement cells.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the already-built renewal processes to the body felt repetitive, even though it brought the chapter together.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the marrow retained dividing cells while new red cells entered the blood, suggesting replacement can continue.

arbitrary.text: Nothing felt purposeless. Connecting marrow and skin in either order was a practical choice, but neither order seemed especially meaningful.

continue.text: I would probably continue for another chapter if it explored another everyday body process; the connected pictures made renewal understandable, though the final fittings felt repetitive.
